QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_49

question.text: Per Ch 4.3.1, the 'learning loop' in the Logic Model enables:

answer.text: Static, one-way execution with no feedback
Feedback flow from outputs / outcomes / impact back into activities and inputs, allowing the project to adapt, refine design, and improve performance over time
Exit of all stakeholders after year 1

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 4.3.1, the learning loop / feedback mechanism in the Logic Model routes information from observed outputs, outcomes and impact back to activities and inputs — enabling adaptive management. A project that doesn't learn fails to correct course and becomes less impactful over time. The SIA should check whether the SE has documented feedback mechanisms. **The Trap:** A denies feedback entirely. C, D are irrelevant. **Cross-Exam Context:** Feedback-loop discipline is tested in XXIII Ch 4/5 (M&E) and parallels plan-do-check-act cycles in management systems auditing. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Ask the SE: 'What did you learn from Year 1 that changed Year 2's design?' If they cannot name three changes, the learning loop is dormant and impact improvement is unlikely.
